      - @1.48s, 1% down: "Video credits: / Andrew Kota / https://www.pexels.com/video/the-cat-scratched-the-wood-3693815/"
      - @1.86s, 18% down: "This second case shows setting both position and tempo. / In score, tempo is simply speed * 120, e.g. a tempo of 120 / is used as reference for "speed of 1". / A step sequencer sets the position (in milliseconds) at regular intervals. / A LFO constantly adjusts speed around that position between -2 and 2 (e.g. tempo -240 and 240.)"
      - @1.86s, 8% down: "This first case shows how to use the tempo curve to adjust / the tempo of an interval. Pay attention to the green progress line, / remember that each interval can have individual tempo."
      - @2.33s, 54% down: "These controls work for any process, including scenario: here, we scrub across a whole set of videos and effects."
      - @2.37s, 36% down: "Exact same thing but with the speed inlet of the Tempo object instead."
      - @19.93s, 35% down: "Notice how the LFO and step sequencer are in a separate interval / than the video: this is because otherwise the speed & position change / would also affect their own rate, leading to unexepected results"
      - @21.01s, 1% down: "This example shows tempo control when video is involved: / it's the same thing that for any other media. / Note that only some video formats support video scrubbing and / reverse playback well: / 1) it's really recommended to convert your video to HAP or an equivalent all-intra format. / 2) in the video inspector, set the playback mode to direct (seek): / it's heavier on the GPU thread but allows frame-accurate seeking / and scrubbing. Use the other mode when you only care about playing a video / file forwards - speed can still be automated, but jumps will have latency and backwards / playback will lag a lot."
      - @26.26s, 18% down: "Note that this works because the step / sequencer sends a message only once per / step. If you have a continuous signal you can use / Rate Limiter or Repetition Filter objects to filter the / incoming stream of data."

### P22 "Echo Trace" (ISF Shader) · Fragment

description: Pixel with brightness levels below the threshold do not update.; categories: Feedback; inputs: inputImage:image, thresh:float=0, gain:float=1, hardCutoff:bool=true, invert:bool=false; passes: 2

```glsl
void main()
{
	vec4		freshPixel = IMG_PIXEL(inputImage,gl_FragCoord.xy);
	vec4		stalePixel = IMG_PIXEL(bufferVariableNameA,gl_FragCoord.xy);
	float		brightLevel = (freshPixel.r + freshPixel.b + freshPixel.g) / 3.0;
	if (invert)
		brightLevel = 1.0 - brightLevel;
	brightLevel = brightLevel * gain;
	if (hardCutoff)	{
		if (brightLevel < thresh)
			brightLevel = 1.0;
		else
			brightLevel = 0.0;
	}
	gl_FragColor = mix(freshPixel,stalePixel, brightLevel);
}
```

### P25 "Multi Feedback" (ISF Shader) · Fragment

description: Feedback with luma key, transform, and hue shift. The input is keyed by brightness, then composited onto a feedback buffer that is continuously panned, zoomed, rotated, and hue-shifted. Produces classic VJ feedback spirals, tunnels, and trails.; categories: Stylize; inputs: inputImage:image, feedback_mix:float=0.85, luma_thresh:float=0.2, luma_soft:float=0.1, fb_zoom:float=0.98, fb_rotate:float=0, fb_pan_x:float=0, fb_pan_y:float=0, fb_hue_shift:float=0, fb_saturation:float=1
